subject: Implementation pathways: blockers, resource asks, and tentative timeline
thread_body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@finapps.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinApps private deployment — quick feasibility note

Ben / team,

Thanks for taking this on. I sketched two high-level implementation pathways for the FinApps VPC/on-prem ask and flagged the main blockers. See attached summary PDF and a quick capacity estimate (excel). High-level:

- Path A (VPC-managed by Redwood): fastest for FinApps, scope includes dedicated tenant in our VPC, routing via NGW, and KMS integration.
- Path B (Customer-managed on-prem / co-lo): much heavier for ops and networking, requires air-gap procedures for backups and support windows.

Blockers we need to resolve before we can give legal / sales a firm timeline:
1) Networking: whether FinApps will accept cross-account peering or requires a transit gateway + explicit ACLs.
2) Security evidence: SOC2 scoping for the dedicated tenant + proposed audit cadence.
3) Resourcing: 0.6 FTE infra lead for 3 months + QA/devtime for model on-boarding.
4) SLA exception: FinApps is asking for 99.95% with a 2-hour support response outside business hours — needs leadership sign-off.

Questions for ops/leadership:
- Can we commit to 0.6 FTE infra for the pilot window or should we surface a contract add-on?
- If we choose Path B, what is the minimum on-call and deployment support we can offer without expanding the support org?

Karen — can you confirm if FinApps requires data to remain in their VPC at rest, or is customer-managed KMS acceptable? That will influence the path selection.

Thanks,
--
Priyom Das
Engineering Lead, Inference Orchestration
Redwood Inference


-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@finapps.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinApps private deployment — quick feasibility note

Priyom,

Appreciate the breakdown — this is exactly the level we need to brief Sales/AE before the contract redlines. A few follow-ups from Product and Finance below so we can close on a recommended path and a tentative timeline: 

- Product (Mina): needs to know the implications for rollout cadence. If we pick Path A, can we support staged rollout by customer region? Any AZ constraints?
- Finance: wants a conservative cost model for both paths so they can price the Managed vs. On-prem options (attach the excel).
- Sales: needs a mutual action plan with dates (pilot start, full onboarding, SLA handover).

Can we get a one-pager that includes: 
  * Required infra FTEs and skillsets (on-call vs project work)
  * Expected lead times for networking approvals and customer-side gatekeeping
  * Minimum test plan to validate 99.95% SLA in a dedicated environment

I'll consolidate and send to AE + FinApps procurement by EOD Monday.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference


On Sun, 21 Mar 2027 at 15:03:00 -0700, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

> Cc: Karen Liu <karen.liu@finapps.com>
> Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Implementation dependencies — product questions
> 
> Ben / team,
> 
> Quick answers to product-level asks:
> 
> - Regional rollout: For Path A (Redwood-managed VPC), we can offer per-region tenancy but it increases infra replication cost ~+18% per secondary region. For pilot we should restrict to us-west-2 unless customer explicitly needs eu/west.
> - AZ constraints: none beyond standard HA architecture (3 AZs recommended).
> - Feature gating: We can gate new model rollouts behind a canary policy tied to the dedicated tenant; that will reduce regression risk during the pilot.
> 
> Product asks for the one-pager: please include the canary gating approach, rollback plan, and a short QA checklist (load test thresholds, percent error budget). I can draft the QA checklist if someone drops the infra capacity numbers in the doc.
> 
> Mina
> Product Director, Core API
> Redwood Inference
> 
> 
> -----Original Message-----
> From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
> Sent: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 20:10:00 -0700
> To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
> Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@finapps.com>
> Subject: Consolidated ask -> Leadership decision (timeline & exceptions)
> 
> Folks,
> 
> I'm looping leadership (Mina/Priyom/Kim) to get two decisions so I can close with FinApps procurement:
> 
> 1) Resource commitment: Approve up to 0.6 FTE infra lead (or indicate that this must be quoted as a time-and-materials add-on).
> 2) SLA exception: Approve 99.95% with 2-hour out-of-hours response for the pilot, or ask sales to push back.
> 
> Quick proposal: Approve the 0.6 FTE for an initial 3-month pilot and accept a conditional SLA exception tied to a paid premium support add-on. If leadership approves, I'll update the MAP and share with FinApps procurement by Monday EOD.
> 
> Action items (owners):
> - Priyom: confirm resource ramp plan + on-call mix (due Mon 09:00 PT)
> - Mina: provide QA checklist bullet points (due Mon 12:00 PT)
> - Kim: confirm whether we can offer region-limited tenancy without extra legal guardrails (due Mon 14:00 PT)
> 
> Karen / FinApps — any flexibility on the out-of-hours response requirement? If you can accept a 4-hour response for non-critical incidents during the pilot, that materially reduces our ops risk.
> 
> Thanks,
> Ben
> 
> --
> Ben Carter
> Director, Solutions Engineering
> Redwood Inference
